dedupe_keys.name: farm flow ag iot security intrusion detection dataset for smart agriculture networks ciic

description: Network traffic from an emulated agricultural Internet of Things (AG-IoT) system, with normal traffic and eight attack types, organised as flows for training intrusion detection models. The Zenodo record says the captures cover three months of traffic, August to October 2022, stored as pcap files cut into 5-second slices, and that the cleaned dataset holds 1,310,000 flow instances (532 MB): 27,458 normal and 1,282,429 attack instances across ARP spoofing, botnet DDoS, HTTP flood, ICMP flood, MQTT flood, port scanning, TCP flood and UDP flood. It reports an intrusion detection accuracy of 92.67 percent and aims to protect data such as crop health, weather and soil conditions. The record was published on 12 April 2024 by five researchers of CIIC as a single downloadable ZIP of about 501 MB, with Captures and Dataset folders, free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is one emulated farm network testbed. Caveats: traffic is emulated, not taken from a working farm, and normal traffic is a small share of the flows. For simulation it gives labelled attack traffic on farm sensor networks, to model how a cyber attack could disrupt irrigation, monitoring and supply chain data. A related catalogue record is AgriEdge, the leakage-free precision agriculture IIoT intrusion benchmark.
